common: One continuous four-second photoreal shot from a locked, fixed-height camera, matching the supplied two-table composition. Keep the lens angle, camera position, field of view, exposure, framing, two table edges, gap, ceramic vessel, shelves and window light fixed. Claire sits behind the far table in the same proportions, blue-gray shirt, dark bangs and gold hoop earrings. She quietly looks directly into this lens from the first to the last frame, lips resting together and with at most one ordinary brief blink. No acting gesture, eye movement off the lens, zoom, pan, tilt, camera travel, cut, resizing or object shift. Keep quiet individual workshop room tone and one soft breath, no dialogue and no music.

variants.A: Keep sharp focus on the lip and glaze of the near ceramic vessel throughout all four seconds. Claire remains softly out of focus.
variants.B: Hold clear focus on the lip and glaze of the near ceramic vessel from 0 to 2 seconds. Between 2 and 3 seconds pull optical focus smoothly once to Claire’s eyes. The vessel and near table soften without shifting. Hold sharp iris and eyelash detail on Claire from 3 to 4 seconds, with no hunting or return.
